resources.string: This standalone app plays speech locally and can save MP3 files. Listening needs no storage access; saving requests the required access when needed.
Arabic: MBROLA AR1/AR2, Flite ASC, and Festival HTS Ziad. These are four actual voice options; quality and pronunciation differ.
Choose the language used by Simple TTS
Text should match the selected voice language
Restore sample text for this voice
This standalone app plays and saves speech locally. Device speech settings are not required for listening or MP3 export.

Flite: 22 local English voices, 5 Arabic voices and 13 Indian-language voices (Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu). Type text in the voice’s own script; Arabic works best with diacritics (Rawi is optional).
Pico: English, German, Spanish, French, and Italian; no Arabic.
rsynth: English only; local formant synthesis.
GnuSpeechSA: one English voice; no Arabic.
Klatt 1980/1990: English formant synthesis; no Arabic.
FreeTTS: American English only; KAL and KAL16 are two voices in the same speaker range, not one recording.

On first launch, grant storage permission (Android 8–10) or enable All files access in Settings (Android 11+). Simple TTS creates its folder automatically at the root of internal shared storage and saves MP3 files there. If you skip access, listening still works; Save can retry later.
Please wait for the current operation to finish.
Optional, runs offline for Arabic voices. Existing vowel marks are preserved; automatic predictions may be wrong.

This standalone app is not available as an Android system TTS engine.

Simple TTS needs storage access to save MP3 files. On Android 11+, All files access is broader than audio access, but Simple TTS writes only its own generated MP3 files and does not read unrelated files. The app creates the Simple TTS folder automatically at the root of internal shared storage. You can listen if you skip this; Save can retry later.
Storage permission was not granted. Listening still works.
Couldn’t open Settings. Enable All files access for Simple TTS in Android settings.
Ziad: Arabic HTS, 48 kHz, GPL-3.0 with corpus CC BY 4.0; optional Rawi. Kurt: American English LPC/diphone, 16 kHz, Edinburgh permissions. Both local; select the matching text language.

Applies to every voice for playback and MP3. On: output at 48 kHz. Off: keep the native sample rate. Selected speed and pitch stay unchanged; native 48 kHz voices remain at 48 kHz in either mode. Resampling does not restore missing detail.
Diacritized text replaced the original in the editor.
The text changed while processing; your edits were kept.
Japanese only. Nitech male HTS voice (2012), fully offline. This engine does not speak Arabic.
Flite + HTS: one American English female voice (CMU ARCTIC SLT) from the statistical HMM family. Local and offline; no Arabic.
Ekho: Hong Kong Cantonese, CantoneseWong recordings; no Arabic or English. Local syllable synthesis with optional 48 kHz output.

System voices: the text-to-speech engines installed on this phone (Google, Samsung, ...) used through Android. They are external, not part of Simple TTS, and may be neural; they may also use the internet according to their own settings. Simple TTS itself has no internet permission and is not a system engine.

These are system voices chosen by you: they may be neural (AI) depending on the installed engine, and the engine itself may use the internet. Speed and pitch are passed to the engine where it supports them.
No other text-to-speech engine is installed on this phone.
Could not load %1$s. Check that the engine is installed and enabled.

Large voices are separate packs so the app stays small. For each pack: 1) download its ZIP from the Simple TTS releases page on GitHub (github.com/alimo7d1133-art/simple-tts-releases, release v1.9.0); 2) unzip it; 3) move the unzipped folder, named like the pack, into the folder “%1$s” in the root of internal storage. Then press Refresh: every file is checked with SHA-256 before the voices are activated. The app has no internet permission and downloads nothing. After activation you may delete the folder you moved.
